title: Method for the mass production of seedlings of the tropical brown seaweed Sargassum (Phaeophyceae, Ochrophyta)
author: Largo, Rance, et al.

steps.title: Assemble filtration tank
steps.instruction: Place a 170 L plastic utility box in the semi‑outdoor facility and fill it sequentially with a bottom layer of gravel, a middle layer of fine sand, an aquarium filter sponge, and a top layer of gravel to create the filtration media.

steps.title: Set up recruitment tanks
steps.instruction: Install plastic utility boxes (72 × 52 × 44 cm) as recruitment tanks, each capable of holding up to 140 L of filtered seawater; connect each tank to the filtration tank and equip with a submersible water pump to aerate and recirculate seawater daily, allowing the tanks to be semi‑exposed to outdoor temperature and light.

steps.title: Supply filtered seawater
steps.instruction: Draw seawater from the adjacent sea, pass it through the filtration tank, and deliver the filtered, aerated water to each recruitment tank, ensuring that no chemical fertilizer or organic biostimulant is added.

steps.title: Prepare clay and limestone panels
steps.instruction: Obtain broken clay pots for clay panels and Mactan stone tiles for limestone panels; these will serve as bottom‑culture substrates.

steps.title: Construct nylon seeding strings
steps.instruction: Acquire 5 mm‑diameter nylon fishing line and wind it tightly around a rectangular PVC frame measuring 48 × 32 cm to create the seeding substrate.

steps.title: Condition substrates in seawater
steps.instruction: Immerse all clay panels, limestone panels, and nylon‑string frames together in seawater for approximately one week to allow natural bacterial film formation.

steps.title: Place substrates in tanks
steps.instruction: In each recruitment tank, place at least 20 conditioned panels (clay or limestone) on the bottom and also position the conditioned nylon‑string frames at the tank bottom; optionally add rough‑sided glass slides alongside panels for microscopic observation of embryos up to the germling stage.

steps.title: Monitor recruitment density
steps.instruction: Periodically count zygotes or seedlings on panels using ImageJ to calculate recruits per cm², and on seeding strings by counting seedlings per area divided by the number of wound strings, to compare attachment efficiency.

steps.title: Out‑plant seedlings after growth
steps.instruction: After more than one year in the tanks, when seedling growth ceases, transfer the seedlings to the sea for out‑planting.
